sources.title: Chronicle of Potosí
sources.author: Bartolomé Arzáns de Orsúa y Vela
sources.excerpt: This mountain of silver has consumed eight million Indian lives in its hellish mines.
sources.longExcerpt: Potosí, richest city in the Americas, built on a mountain of silver and indigenous blood. The Cerro Rico has yielded enough silver to build a bridge to Spain, they say. But at what cost? Eight million Indians have died in these mines, chewing coca leaves to survive the altitude, the cold, the sixteen-hour shifts. The city has 160,000 souls, 36 churches, 14 dance halls, 800 professional gamblers. Prices exceed those of Paris. A chicken costs eight reales, an Indian life is worth nothing.

citation.originalPublication: Bartolomé Arzáns de Orsúa y Vela, 1705
